item.title: China tightens security in Shenzhen ahead of APEC Summit, detains citizens and restricts residents
item.description: Chinese authorities have intensified security measures across Shenzhen ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, with reports of citizen detentions, forced ...
item.content:encoded:
China tightens security in Shenzhen ahead of APEC Summit, detains citizens and restricts residents Chinese authorities have intensified security measures across Shenzhen ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, with reports of citizen detentions, forced temporary relocations of residents and disruptions to daily life, according to a report by The Epoch Times (TET). ANI | Updated: 18-11-2026 18:17 IST | Created: 18-11-2026 18:17 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Chinese authorities have intensified security measures across Shenzhen ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, with reports of citizen detentions, forced temporary relocations of residents and disruptions to daily life, according to a report by The Epoch Times (TET). The APEC summit, involving 21 member economies, is scheduled to take place in Shenzhen on November 18–19. US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are also expected to hold a trilateral meeting on the final day, the report stated. According to TET, the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department held a province-wide mobilisation meeting on November 1 to coordinate security operations. Police personnel from across Guangdong were reportedly reassigned to Shenzhen, with intensified patrols, pedestrian checks, perimeter security and increased surveillance around key locations. Residents told the publication that police conducted random identity checks on pedestrians on November 3, while security inspections across the Shenzhen Metro were also tightened. Yang Fan, a Shenzhen-based white-collar worker who spoke under a pseudonym fearing reprisals, told TET that the city had entered what he described as "APEC time", with noticeable restrictions on everyday activities. He said streets had become unusually quiet and traffic controls had become significantly stricter. The report also highlighted a citywide ban on vehicle horns introduced from November 1 by the Shenzhen Municipal Bureau of Ecology and Environment and the municipal traffic police. The restriction is scheduled to remain in force for five years, with violations subject to legal penalties. Yang further said several companies, particularly in the high-tech industrial hub of Nanshan, had instructed employees to work remotely, resulting in fewer commuters. TET also cited social media posts alleging that some residents were prevented from returning to their homes during the summit preparations. Certain residential buildings were reportedly placed under lockdown, with security personnel stationed at entrances. Affected households were allegedly offered daily compensation of 600 yuan (approximately USD 90). Yang confirmed that residents living near the summit venue at Xiangmi Lake had been instructed to relocate temporarily, with some reportedly transferred to designated hotels. Yang alleged that authorities were also placing individuals with no apparent connection to petitioning activities under preventive "stability maintenance" measures. The report noted that these restrictions reflect the expanded security arrangements surrounding the APEC summit, with residents experiencing increased surveillance and disruptions to normal life. (ANI)

item.title: Andhra Pradesh unveils semiconductor policy with up to 80% capital support, plans 5,000-acre chip park in Tirupati
item.description: Andhra Pradesh has unveiled its new Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy 4.0, offering up to 80 per cent capital support for semiconductor fabrication units and proposing a dedicated 5,000-acre ...
item.content:encoded:
Andhra Pradesh unveils semiconductor policy with up to 80% capital support, plans 5,000-acre chip park in Tirupati Andhra Pradesh has unveiled its new Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy 4.0, offering up to 80 per cent capital support for semiconductor fabrication units and proposing a dedicated 5,000-acre semiconductor park in Tirupati to attract investments across the chip manufacturing value chain. ANI | Updated: 18-11-2026 16:27 IST | Created: 18-11-2026 16:27 IST

Representative image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Andhra Pradesh has unveiled its new Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy 4.0, offering up to 80 per cent capital support for semiconductor fabrication units and proposing a dedicated 5,000-acre semiconductor park in Tirupati to attract investments across the chip manufacturing value chain. Announcing the policy in a post on X, Andhra Pradesh Minister for Information Technology, Electronics and Communications, Nara Lokesh, said the state would match 100 per cent of the Centre's support under India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) 2.0. "Big news for India's chip ambitions! Andhra Pradesh's new Semiconductor & Display Fab Policy 4.0 is here," Lokesh said. Highlighting the financial incentives, he said, "With the Centre and State together, silicon fabs get 80% support, and compound, photonics, sensor, display and advanced packaging units get 70%. That's the highest in the country, ahead of Odisha and Tamil Nadu (65%), UP and MP (60%) and Gujarat (56%)." The state government also plans to develop a dedicated semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem in Tirupati, equipped with infrastructure required for chip fabrication and allied industries. "We are building a dedicated 5,000-acre AP Semiconductor Park at Tirupati, with cleanrooms, redundant high-voltage power, ultrapure water, specialty gases, testing labs and logistics. It will be a cluster for the full value chain," Lokesh said. According to the minister, the policy covers all 10 categories under Semicon 2.0, including chip design, machinery and materials, fabrication, assembly, testing, marking and packaging (ATMP), outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT), research and development, and talent development. Design startups will be eligible for seed funding of up to Rs 22.5 crore, while research and development and talent-related projects will receive state support equivalent to 25 per cent of project costs. The policy also proposes a single-window mechanism through the AP Semiconductor Growth and Innovation Council, chaired by Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu. A new research centre focusing on photonics will also be established at IIT Tirupati. On workforce development, Lokesh said, "The new AP Semiconductor Training Centre in the Park will offer ₹10,000 per trainee per month for 6 months, with curricula designed with industry and our universities." Inviting investments, he added, "Andhra Pradesh wants to be the place where India builds its chips, from design to fab to packaging. Come build with us." Meanwhile, the Centre's Semicon 2.0 initiative aims to strengthen India's semiconductor ecosystem through six key pillars, including chip design, machinery and materials, fabrication facilities, ATMP/OSAT operations, research and development, and talent development. Under the initiative, the government aims to deepen the chip design ecosystem, with 105 startups already developing chips, while encouraging investments in semiconductor manufacturing equipment, materials, chemicals and gases. The programme also seeks to attract additional fabrication facilities, including silicon, compound semiconductor and display fabs, with India's first semiconductor fab scheduled to be commissioned in 2028. On talent development, the initiative builds on existing efforts under which around 68,000 students across 315 universities have received training in complex chip design using electronic design automation tools. Semicon 2.0 also aims to advance semiconductor research beyond the initial 28nm-110nm technology nodes and strengthen India's supply chain resilience, technological capabilities and domestic semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem. (ANI)

item.title: Xi, Putin pledge stable ties ahead of trilateral meeting with US in Shenzhen
item.description: Meeting in Shenzhen on Wednesday ahead of their trilateral summit with the US, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin pledged to strengthen bilateral ties and promote a ...
item.content:encoded:
Xi, Putin pledge stable ties ahead of trilateral meeting with US in Shenzhen Meeting in Shenzhen on Wednesday ahead of their trilateral summit with the US, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin pledged to strengthen bilateral ties and promote a multipolar world order. Xi also addressed the APEC CEO Summit, urging open trade and regional cooperation. ANI | Updated: 18-11-2026 11:23 IST | Created: 18-11-2026 11:23 IST

Russian President Vladimir Putin with Chinese President Xi Jinping (File Photo/Reuters) . Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday, where they pledged to preserve stable bilateral ties and drive a multipolar global order amid mounting international uncertainties, ahead of their landmark trilateral meeting with the United States. Emphasising the robust character of their partnership, Xi remarked that China-Russia relations "stand as firm as a mountain amid wind and rain," urging both sides to adopt a long-term strategic outlook to instil greater stability and certainty into global affairs. "Russian-Chinese political cooperation is working favourably and constructively in a difficult political situation," Putin stated. "We are committed to constructive approaches to form a fairer multipolar world order," he added. The Russian leader touched down in Shenzhen just before 2 am on Wednesday, receiving a ceremonial tarmac welcome from Cai Qi, China's fifth-ranking official, marking the highest-level airport reception accorded to any visiting leader at the APEC gathering thus far. According to Russian media reports, Putin's busy itinerary in Shenzhen encompasses the inaugural Russia-China-US leaders' summit, formal APEC sessions, and a scheduled visit to Shenzhen MSU-BIT University. Alongside the historic trilateral meeting, marking a first among the three heads of state, an envisaged separate bilateral meeting between Putin and US President Donald Trump is also lined up, in addition to talks with the leaders of several other nations. The White House stated that the upcoming discussions are expected to focus on curbing the proliferation of nuclear weapons against the backdrop of ongoing conflicts in Iran and Ukraine. President Trump earlier remarked that the leaders would discuss denuclearisation, which he described as a "tough subject", as well as the situations in Iran and Ukraine. Earlier on Wednesday, addressing the APEC CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen, President Xi stated that China is willing to collaborate with all parties to forge ahead with greater confidence and resolve to jointly build an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together. Xi urged the region to expand pathways to mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. He stressed that concrete efforts should be made to eliminate trade and investment barriers to foster an open Asia-Pacific economy, while simultaneously promoting inclusive and balanced development to ensure both efficiency and fairness. (ANI)
